title: Normal text contrast ≥ 4.5:1
summary: All normal text must meet WCAG AA 4.5:1 (antislop R-25; antislop-human 'Low-Contrast Text'; Claude design-system-prompt contrast chapter; pa11y audits WCAG2AA by default). Light grey text on white is the most common miss.

source.rule: R-25 Color Contrast (4.5:1 normal text)
Low-Contrast Text (compute the ratio, do not eyeball)
Contrast (WCAG): normal text under 18px minimum 4.5:1
Automated accessibility testing; WCAG2AA default standard

notes: Contrast is local: test every spot text passes over, including over images and gradients. Use the WCAG formula ((L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05)) or a checker; never eyeball.

title: Large text contrast ≥ 3:1
summary: Large text (18px+ bold or 24px+ regular) needs only 3:1 per WCAG AA (antislop R-25; Claude design-system-prompt; Hallmark gate 40 thresholds).

params.window: large text pair (>=18px bold or >=24px regular)

source.rule: R-25 (large text 18px+ minimum 3:1)
Large text (18px+ bold or 24px+): minimum 3:1
Gate 40 contrast thresholds (large text WCAG 3:1)

title: Non-text UI contrast ≥ 3:1
summary: Component boundaries, icons, input borders, focus indicators, and status indicators need 3:1 against adjacent colors (WCAG 1.4.11; antislop-human 'Non-Text Contrast'; Claude design-system-prompt UI components 3:1; Hallmark gate 40 includes focus rings at 3:1).

source.rule: Non-Text Contrast (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11)
UI components (buttons, icons): minimum 3:1
Gate 40 (icons and focus rings need WCAG 3:1)

title: No contrast claims without computation
summary: The grey-on-grey hallucination: claiming a pairing passes AA without running the math (antislop-human). '#555555 on black is 2.8:1 — it fails'; the eye overestimates contrast on grey pairs and agents repeat the claim because it sounds plausible.

source.rule: The Grey-on-Grey Hallucination

tests.label: uncomputed claim fails
tests.input: This #555555 on black easily passes AA contrast.

tests.label: computed verdict passes
tests.input: #777777 on white is 4.48:1, which fails the 4.5:1 threshold for normal text.

notes: Never assert a pairing passes; run the contrast checker or the formula. #555555 on black computes to 2.8:1.

title: Text over photo/gradient: verify the worst spot
summary: White text over an image or gradient that is light in some areas drops below 4.5:1 where the image is light; checking one bright spot only is the tell (antislop-human 'Text Over a Photo or Gradient'; antislop R-25 requires testing the whole area).

source.rule: Text Over a Photo or Gradient / R-25 (test the whole area, not one point)

tests.label: single-spot check fails
tests.input: White headline over a hero photo, contrast verified only at the dark corner.

tests.label: scrim + worst spot passes
tests.input: Headline over a scrim; verified the lightest part of the image still clears 4.5:1.

title: Never remove the focus outline
summary: `outline: none` or `outline: 0` with no replacement focus style removes the only keyboard visibility indicator; banned by antislop R-32, antislop-human, and the Claude design-system-prompt ('one of the most common accessibility failures').

source.rule: R-32 Keyboard Accessibility (FORBIDDEN outline: none without replacement)
Removed Focus Outline
Never remove the focus ring; replace it with :focus-visible

title: Focus indicator must be visible and 3:1
summary: A focus ring the same color as the background, one that only appears on hover, or one thinner than a 1px border fails the contrast bar (antislop-human 'Weak or Invisible Focus Indicator'); Hallmark gate 26 requires :focus-visible, :active, and :disabled styling on every interactive element.

source.rule: Weak or Invisible Focus Indicator (R-32, R-34)
Gate 26: interactive element lacks :focus-visible / :active / :disabled

tests.label: invisible focus fails
tests.input: button:focus { outline-color: #FFFFFF; } /* white ring on a white page */

notes: Check the indicator in every theme you ship, light and dark (R-34). Focus rings must also appear instantly — no fade-in (Hallmark gate 15).

title: No mouse-only interactions
summary: Menus that open on hover only, dropdowns that click-open but do not keyboard-open, drag-and-drop with no keyboard fallback: each excludes keyboard and assistive-tech users (antislop-human 'Mouse-Only Patterns'; Claude design-system-prompt keyboard navigation; antislop R-32).

source.rule: Mouse-Only Patterns (R-32)
Keyboard navigation: everything reachable and operable by keyboard; hover-only interactions fail

tests.label: hover-only menu fails
tests.input: Dropdown opens on :hover only; Enter/Space do nothing when the trigger is focused.

tests.label: keyboard-operable passes
tests.input: Dropdown opens on click or Enter/Space and navigates with arrow keys; Esc closes it.

title: Logical tab order; dialogs close on Escape
summary: Focus that jumps around, skips content, or lands on hidden elements because DOM order does not match visual order makes navigation unpredictable (antislop-human 'Broken Tab Order'); modals must close on Escape (Claude design-system-prompt; antislop R-32).

source.rule: Broken Tab Order (R-32)
Modals must close on Escape; tab order must be logical

tests.label: scattered tabindex fails
tests.input: tabindex="5" on the footer link, tabindex="1" on a hidden sidebar — focus jumps past main content.

tests.label: source-order passes
tests.input: DOM order matches visual order; skip link jumps to main; modal traps focus and closes on Escape.

notes: Never give real content tabindex="-1" unless part of a controlled focus trap such as a dialog.

title: Interactive hit targets ≥ 44px
summary: Tap/click targets smaller than 44px × 44px exclude touch and low-precision users (antislop R-03 minimum tap target 44px; Claude design-system-prompt 'interactive hit targets: never smaller than 44px × 44px').

source.rule: R-03 (button sizes meet the minimum tap target 44px)
Interactive hit targets: never smaller than 44px × 44px

title: No color-only status feedback
summary: Success/error/status communicated only by color excludes color-blind and low-vision users and disappears in forced-colors mode (antislop-human 'Color-Only Feedback'; Claude design-system-prompt 'don't rely on color alone to communicate state').

source.rule: Color-Only Feedback (C-4)
Don't rely on color alone to communicate state — pair with icons, text, or position

tests.label: red border only fails
tests.input: input.invalid { border-color: red; } /* no message, no icon */

tests.label: text-first error passes
tests.input: "Password must be at least 8 characters" shown beside the red-bordered field.

title: Motion must have a prefers-reduced-motion fallback
summary: Every animation/transition needs a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) alternative (Claude design-system-prompt Motion; Hallmark gate 27: any transform/animation keyframe not covered by the fallback fails).

source.rule: Respect prefers-reduced-motion
Gate 27: every transform/animation keyframe covered by prefers-reduced-motion

tests.label: uncovered animation fails
tests.input: .card { transition: transform 0.3s ease; } /* no reduced-motion media query in the stylesheet */

title: Use semantic HTML, not div-on-click
summary: Buttons are <button>, links are <a>, structure uses <nav>/<main>/<article>; ARIA is a patch for when semantic HTML can't express the role (Claude design-system-prompt 'Semantic HTML'; pa11y/axe audits flag role misuse).

source.rule: Semantic HTML: <button> for buttons, never <div onclick>; proper heading hierarchy
Runs axe-core / HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG audits

notes: Also covers heading hierarchy: don't skip levels (<h1> to <h3>).

title: Alt text on meaningful images
summary: Every meaningful image needs descriptive alt text; decorative images get alt=""; missing alt fails screen-reader and automated audits (Claude design-system-prompt screen-reader support; pa11y example: 'Img element is the only content of the link, but is missing alt text').

source.rule: Alt text on every meaningful image; empty alt for decorative
Audits alt-text violations (HTML_CodeSniffer example result)

tests.label: descriptive alt passes

notes: Decorative images use alt="" so screen readers skip them.

title: Labels on every form input
summary: Placeholder text is not a label — it disappears when the user types (Claude design-system-prompt form design; 'labels on every form input').

source.rule: Labels on every form input; placeholder is not a label

tests.label: placeholder-only fails
tests.input: <input placeholder="Email address"> with no <label for> or aria-label.

notes: Use type="email"/"tel" and autocomplete attributes for mobile keyboards and autofill.

title: Text must reflow at 200% zoom
summary: Fixed pixel font sizes and overflow:hidden containers that clip text at 200% zoom break WCAG 1.4.4 text resizing (antislop-human 'Text That Cannot Zoom', R-35).

source.rule: Text That Cannot Zoom (WCAG 1.4.4, R-35)

tests.label: clipped at zoom fails
tests.input: body { font-size: 12px; } .copy { overflow: hidden; height: 200px; } /* text clips at 200% zoom */

tests.label: fluid type passes
tests.input: body { font-size: clamp(16px, 1rem + 0.5vw, 20px); } /* reflows at 200% zoom on a narrow viewport */

title: Focus indicator at least 2px or equivalent area
summary: A custom focus indicator thinner than 2px — outline: 1px, outline: thin — fails the visible-area bar for keyboard users (better-accessibility: 'Use at least a 2px solid perimeter or an equivalent visible area'; WCAG 2.4.7 minimum 2px per wcag-accessibility-audit).

source.rule: Visible Focus Rings — at least 2px solid perimeter or equivalent visible area
Focus rings — custom outline: 2px solid; never thinner
2.4.7 Focus Visible — minimum 2px, high contrast

notes: Works with ZS-A11Y-006 (never outline: none) and ZS-A11Y-007 (the ring's contrast must be verified against every adjacent color). A 2px+ outline is the floor; verify the complete indicator in every theme, including forced-colors mode.

title: sr-only must hide visually, not from assistive tech
summary: An .sr-only / .visually-hidden class implemented with display: none or visibility: hidden removes the content from assistive tech entirely — the pattern hides from everyone (better-accessibility screen-readers: 'Never use display:none or visibility:hidden for this; both remove the content from assistive tech entirely').

source.rule: Visually hidden content — canonical .sr-only pattern; never display:none or visibility:hidden

tests.label: canonical clip pattern passes
tests.input: .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; }

notes: Use 1px boxes, not 0 — some screen readers skip zero-sized elements. white-space: nowrap prevents words from being read as one run-together string. Skip links add a focus variant that un-hides the element (:focus overrides the positioning).

title: Autoplaying media needs visible controls
summary: Media that moves, blinks, or updates automatically for more than 5 seconds needs a visible pause/stop control (WCAG 2.2.2); muted looping hero videos included (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom: 'No autoplaying media without visible controls').

source.rule: No autoplaying media without visible controls (WCAG 2.2.2)
2.2.2 auto-playing media with controls

notes: Under prefers-reduced-motion, kill autoplay entirely and start carousels paused. Media without sound that runs longer than 5 seconds still needs the pause control — duration is the trigger, not audio.

title: Auto-dismiss timers need a 5-second floor
summary: Auto-dismissing toasts that time out in under 5 seconds give users no window to act; 5 seconds is the floor, and hovering or focusing the toast must pause the timer (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom: 'If a toast must time out, 5 seconds is the floor').

source.rule: Autoplay and timed UI — 5 second floor; hover/focus pauses the timer

notes: Flags dismiss-style timers under 5000ms. Not every setTimeout is a dismissal timer — review hits in context. Low-stakes confirmations may auto-dismiss; anything containing an action, an error, or information the user may need to act on stays until dismissed.

title: Toasts need a live region to announce
summary: A toast with no aria-live or role is invisible to screen readers — the only way to convey the information fails (fixing-accessibility: 'toasts must not be the only way to convey critical information'; better-accessibility: toasts belong in a polite role="status" live region).

source.rule: Toasts must not be the only way to convey critical information
Announce Dynamic Content — polite live region (role="status") for toasts
Live regions — role="status" for toasts, role="alert" for urgent errors

notes: Default to polite (role="status"); reserve role="alert" / aria-live="assertive" for urgent errors not tied to a control. The 'only path to an action inside an auto-dismissing toast' variant — data loss on a schedule — is semantic and deferred to M3.

title: Placeholder is not a label
summary: An input with placeholder= but no accessible name attribute leaves the field unlabeled — placeholder text disappears the moment the user types (better-accessibility forms: 'A placeholder is never a label'; fixing-accessibility: every input must be labeled).

source.rule: Labels — placeholder is never a label
Every input, select, and textarea must be labeled

notes: The regex inspects the input element only; a linked <label for> or wrapping label also satisfies but is a cross-element association (see semantic ZS-A11Y-015). Placeholders used in addition to a label are fine and show an example of the expected format.

title: No fixed min-width blocking 320px reflow
summary: A fixed min-width of 800px or more on a container forces horizontal scrolling at the 320px equivalent (400% zoom on a 1280px viewport), breaking WCAG 1.4.10 reflow — content must work with vertical scrolling only (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom; wcag-accessibility-audit 1.4.10).

source.rule: Reflow at 320px — no two-dimensional scrolling
1.4.10 Reflow — content reflows to 320px width without horizontal scrolling

notes: min-width is the blocker; max-width is fine. Genuinely two-dimensional content (tables, maps, code blocks) scrolls inside its own container — that is the 2D-content exception, not a page-level min-width. Fixed heights on text containers are the same failure mode under 200% zoom: prefer min-height.

title: No forced-color-adjust: none without system colors
summary: forced-color-adjust: none freezes the authored color in Windows High Contrast mode, defeating the user's forced-colors palette (better-accessibility focus-and-keyboard: 'never freeze the authored color with forced-color-adjust: none unless the control remains perceivable').

source.rule: Forced-colors — keep default color adjustment or use a system color such as Highlight

notes: In forced-colors: active, keep the default color adjustment or explicitly use a system color (Highlight, ButtonText, CanvasText). Custom focus colors must be re-verified under forced colors, not frozen.

title: No positive tabindex values
summary: Positive tabindex hijacks the tab order for the whole page, jumping focus past content in DOM order; only tabindex="0" (join natural order) and tabindex="-1" (programmatic focus) are valid (better-accessibility focus-and-keyboard: 'Positive tabindex: never. It hijacks the tab order for the whole page; fix the DOM order instead').

source.rule: tabindex rules — only 0 and -1, never positive values
Do not use tabindex greater than 0

notes: Concrete, machine-checkable half of the semantic broken-tab-order rule (ZS-A11Y-009): fix the DOM order instead of patching with positive values. Roving tabindex for composite widgets: active item 0, all others -1.

title: Never aria-hidden a focusable element
summary: aria-hidden="true" on a focusable element creates tab stops that don't exist for screen readers — elements you can Tab to that are invisible to assistive tech (better-accessibility: 'Never put it on (or above) a focusable element; that creates stops you can Tab to that don't exist for a screen reader').

source.rule: Never put aria-hidden on (or above) a focusable element
aria-hidden — never on a focusable element

notes: If you hide something interactive, also remove it from the tab order (and from focusability). Decorative elements get aria-hidden="true" only when they are genuinely non-focusable.

title: No aria-label on role-less div or span
summary: aria-label on a plain <div> or <span> is ignored by most screen readers — names on non-interactive, role-less elements do nothing (better-accessibility semantics-and-aria: 'Names on non-interactive, role-less elements are ignored by most screen readers').

source.rule: Common ARIA mistakes — aria-label on a plain div or span

notes: aria-label only works on elements with a role or native naming. The real fix is usually a native element — <button>, <a>, <nav> — rather than ARIA on a div.

title: Icon-only buttons need accessible names
summary: An icon-only button with no aria-label or aria-labelledby has no accessible name — screen readers announce nothing or read the file name (fixing-accessibility: 'icon-only buttons must have aria-label or aria-labelledby'; better-accessibility: 'Icon-only buttons need a descriptive aria-label').

source.rule: Icon-only buttons must have aria-label or aria-labelledby
Accessible Names Everywhere — icon-only buttons need a descriptive aria-label

notes: The icon inside a labeled button should be aria-hidden="true" so the name isn't doubled. A visible text label inside the button also satisfies the rule (text-first buttons don't match this pattern); aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label works too.
